channel.title: Israel National News Flashes
channel.description: Latest news flashes from Israel National News

item.title: Reports in Austria: Missing Israelis may have fled voluntarily to South America
item.description:
Austrian reports suggest the two missing Israelis left voluntarily, as police map their timeline and the family urges authorities to investigate all possibilities.
(Arutz Sheva-Israel National News' North American desk is keeping you updated until the start of Shabbat in New York. The time posted automatically on all Israel National News articles, however, is Israeli time.)

item.title: Shabbat Shalom from Israel!
item.description:
Arutz Sheva-Israel National News' Israel desk is stopping its round-the-clock news updates at this time in honor of Shabbat. Jerusalem candle lighting time is 18:44 on Friday. Our North American desk will keep you informed until the 19:37 EDT candle lighting time in New York.
The updates from Israel will resume Saturday night, following the conclusion of Shabbat at 20:01 in Jerusalem.
Shabbat Shalom!

item.title: Amb. Leiter: “What we saw in the village of Qusra is not what it means to settle the land"
item.description: Israel’s Ambassador to the US Yechiel Leiter condemned violence in Qusra, saying settling the Land of Israel must be rooted in justice and the rule of law.

item.title: Staff sergeant Nave Habshoosh's grandfather hospitalized in intensive care
item.description:
The grandfather of Staff sergeant Nave Habshoosh z"l, from the community of Adam, a fighter and tank commander in the 52nd Battalion of the 401st Brigade who fell in battle in southern Lebanon, has been hospitalized in an intensive care unit, in serious condition.
The family is asking the public to pray for his recovery, saying that since the death of his grandson, he has struggled to return to his daily routine and has barely eaten.
Full name: Eli Trozman ben Louiza

item.title: Mein Kampf found at new London Arabic bookstore sparks outrage
item.description: Copies of Hitler’s Mein Kampf in Arabic found at a London bookstore have triggered accusations of antisemitism, while the store’s owners dispute claims that the book was prominently displayed.

item.title: Significant easing of congestion at Ben Gurion Airport, luggage arriving within minutes
item.description: The Israel Airports Authority reports a significant easing of congestion at Ben Gurion Airport and a substantial reduction in luggage unloading times. On all flights, luggage is now arriving at the baggage carousels within just a few minutes.

item.title: Attorney General sends message to haredi educational networks
item.description: The Attorney General submitted the state’s response to the High Court of Justice, indicating that funding for haredi education networks would be conditional on meeting full core objectives and on close supervision.

item.title: Moments before his phone died, a tourist was rescued in the Judean Desert
item.description: The 20-year-old left a festival near Tekoa, lost his way toward the Judean Desert, and reported to police that he had no water. Volunteers from the Etzion-Yehuda rescue unit rescued him from the Tekoa riverbed.

item.title: Suspected: Chinese money used to support pro-Palestinian protests
item.description: US officials are examining allegations that funds from a network linked to China reached bodies involved in pro-Palestinian protests in the UK.

item.title: 90,000 passengers and an unusual backlog of flights
item.description: Unusual backlog of 90 flights within three hours causes congestion at Ben Gurion Int'l Airport. Israel Airports Authority blames restrictions in Europe and US refueling aircraft, 'There is no shortage of workers.'

item.title: New evidence in case of missing Israelis in Vienna
item.description: Security cameras captured the mother and daughter leaving the apartment where they were staying in Vienna, carrying their belongings and with no one else accompanying them.

item.title: Yisrael Beytenu: Another murder threat directed at Liberman on TikTok
item.description: The Yisrael Beytenu party announced that another murder threat was made on TikTok against the party's chairman, MK Avigdor Liberman. Following the threat, a complaint was filed with the Knesset officer and the police. The party claims that a "wave of threats" has recently been made against Liberman and his family.

item.title: MK Elazar Stern resigns from Knesset
item.description: Elazar Stern informed Lapid that he will resign from the Knesset after 11 years as a Yesh Atid MK, apparently ahead of a possible run with Eisenkot's party.

item.title: MK Simcha Rothman: 'Reserve duty burden must be shared by more people'
item.description: Religious Zionism MK says gradual haredi enlistment could ease burden on reservists and enable more soldiers to return to their families, calls for 61-seat right-wing majority that is loyal to the national camp.

item.title: Israeli Consul: 'Mamdani is failing to protect New York Jewish community'
item.description: Israeli Consul General in New York, Ofir Akunis reacts to rise in antisemitic hate crimes in NYC since Zohran Mamdani became mayor.

item.title: Troops bust attempt to smuggle 50 kg of drugs across eastern border
item.description:
More than 50 kilograms of drugs, estimated to be worth millions of shekels, were discovered yesterday during searches along Israel’s eastern border in the Jordan Valley area.
According to the IDF, the drugs were found in sacks by troops from the Lions of the Jordan Battalion and trackers from the Jordan Valley and Emekim Brigade. They were handed over to police for further investigation.
In recent months, security forces have foiled smuggling attempts involving more than 200 kilograms of drugs in the area.

item.title: After 11 years: Elazar Stern to resign from the Knesset
item.description: Yesh Atid Chairman, former Prime Minister Yair Lapid, announced that MK Elazar Stern informed him of his intention to resign from the Knesset after 11 years as a Yesh Atid MK.

item.title: Airports Authority explains major delays at Ben Gurion Airport
item.description:
The Israel Airports Authority rejected reports of a staffing shortage at Ben Gurion International Airport, saying the delays were caused, among other factors, by heavy air traffic, restrictions in European airspace, and flights by American refueling aircraft.
According to the authority, an unusually large backlog of approximately 90 flights accumulated within three hours, while around 90,000 passengers are expected to pass through the airport today.

item.title: Spanish broadcasters snubbed Israeli runner on live TV
item.description: Video circulating on social media appears to show Spanish broadcasters refusing to introduce an Israeli runner during a track-and-field event, prompting accusations of anti-Israel bias.

item.description: Arutz Sheva learns plans to shift civil enforcement in Area C to police could require doubling the Judea and Samaria force to about 3,000 officers.

item.title: Tanker struck by UAV while leaving Strait of Hormuz
item.description: UKMTO has received reports from Military Authorities that a tanker was struck by a UAV whilst conducting an outbound transit of the Strait of Hormuz. The vessel was subject to minor damage; the crew are reported as safe and accounted for, and no environmental impact has been reported.

item.description: After receiving a report of gunfire on a vehicle, police raid complex and find M-16 assault rifle hiding in preschool sandbox.

item.description: Hashem adjures us to ‘cleave to Him’ - and as Hashem is upright and righteous, one who wants to cleave to Him, has to also be ‘upright and righteous’.

item.title: A note on the Catholic Church's mini-October 7th
item.description: The outcry over Hamel’s killing lasted only as long as it took for the ink on the page the following day to dry. And Pope Francis, after Hamel’s murder, said: “If I speak of Islamic violence I must also speak of Catholic violence." He really said that. Opinion.
